extracted.intended_audience: reporters, journalists, content creators, and communicators who cover or may report on people with disabilities or disability issues
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for journalists and content creators to improve, expand, and accurately report on disability issues and people with disabilities, including language use, interviewing practices, and evaluation/recognition of coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalistic principle of accuracy in news coverage of disability issues and people with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NCDJ is concerned with the journalistic principle of accuracy (it does not advocate a particular point of view); resources aim to help reporters be factually correct when covering disability-related topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalistic principle of fairness in coverage of disability issues and individuals with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources and guidance emphasize fair representation and treatment of people with disabilities in reporting, avoiding misrepresentation and bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity in news coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure diverse representation and inclusion of people with disabilities, who are the largest marginalized group but remain underrepresented and often misrepresented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The center's goal is to help expand and improve coverage of disability issues to increase representation and correct misrepresentation across news, entertainment, sports and other platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutrality / non-advocacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain journalistic neutrality rather than advocating a particular point of view when reporting on disability issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NCDJ states it does not advocate a particular point of view and focuses on journalistic principles (accuracy, fairness, diversity) as the basis for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disability language and terminology (Style Guide)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use recommended language and disability-related terms as set out in the NCDJ's comprehensive Disability Language Style Guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The center offers a comprehensive Disability Language Style Guide with recommendations about language and disability-related terms to guide reporters on appropriate, respectful usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practices for interviewing people with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow recommended interviewing practices when speaking with people with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NCDJ provides tip sheets with best practices for interviewing people with disabilities to ensure respectful, effective information-gathering and portrayal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality recognition in disability coverage (contest)
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional standards exemplified by an annual journalism contest devoted exclusively to disability coverage that recognizes exemplary work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NCDJ hosts the only professional journalism contest devoted exclusively to disability coverage — an annual celebration of the best work across the globe — signaling standards of exemplary reporting in the field.
